name: Decision Log (ADR)
blurb: short records of why a part or topology was chosen
intro: Architecture Decision Records in Michael Nygard's form - context, decision, alternatives, consequences - one row each, saved as the project's record in the app. It checks IDs, ISO dates and the superseded-by chain, flags records missing a part, and writes the log as Markdown.

inputs.label: Decisions
inputs.help: Never rewrite an accepted row: add a new one and set the old one to superseded, with the new ID in Superseded by.

default.title: USB-C 5 V input, no barrel jack
default.context: Desk fan, users have USB chargers; 5 V at under 1.5 A is enough for fan and logic.
default.decision: Power from a USB-C receptacle with 5.1 kΩ CC pull-downs (sink, default USB power).
default.alternatives: Barrel jack 12 V: needs a wall adapter and a bigger buck. USB-C PD: extra controller for power we do not need.
default.consequences: Max 5 V x 1.5 A; fan must be a 5 V type. Needs ESD protection on VBUS and CC.

default.title: Buck converter for 3V3
default.context: 5 V to 3.3 V at up to 300 mA for the ESP32-C3 radio bursts.
default.alternatives: LDO: 0.51 W lost at 300 mA and the board gets warm in a closed case.
default.consequences: Needs a careful layout of the switch node; one more inductor on the BOM.

default.title: 0.96 inch 128x64 OLED
default.context: A small status display for speed and temperature.
default.consequences: Needs a 27 x 28 mm window in the case.

default.title: 128x32 OLED instead of 128x64
default.context: The case was shrunk to pocket size; the 128x64 window no longer fits.
default.decision: SSD1306 128x32, same I2C bus and driver.
default.alternatives: Keep 128x64 and grow the case: rejected, size matters more.
default.consequences: Two lines of text instead of four; firmware layout changes.

default.title: Heat-set inserts for the lid screws
default.context: The lid is opened for service; screws straight into PLA wear out.
default.decision: M3 brass heat-set inserts in the base.

usage: Pass `decisions` as rows {id, date (YYYY-MM-DD), title, status: proposed|accepted|rejected|deprecated|superseded, context, decision, alternatives, consequences, superseded_by}; `status` filters (all, active, or one status) and `filter` searches every field. It returns the index table, the records missing context/alternatives/consequences, the next free ID and all records as Markdown ADRs, with warnings for duplicate IDs, bad dates and broken or looping superseded-by links. Read the project's log with the MCP tool tool_data (id decision-log) before proposing a part or topology change, and add a record (data {decisions: [...]}) when you make one.
sources: Michael Nygard, "Documenting Architecture Decisions" (2011) - the ADR form
MADR - Markdown Any Decision Records (adr.github.io/madr): considered options
